C0.quote: This paper investigates the manipulative power of the polling agency.
C0.note: Manipulation of iterative plurality/veto elections via opinion polls.

C1.quote: Several restricted variants are considered with respect to their parameterized complexity.
C1.note: Complexity of poll manipulation (a strategic-behaviour problem) plus simulations of heuristics on impartial culture.

C2.1.value: ballot; profile of ballots (rule applied to b); preference profile held separately
C2.1.quote: each voter i is asked to submit a ballot bi ∈ M

C2.2.quote: submit a ballot bi ∈ M corresponding to a single candidate
C2.2.note: Ballot is a single candidate (approved under plurality, vetoed under veto).

C2.3.quote: Each voter i has strict ordinal preferences over the candidates

C2.4.quote: A profile of ballots is said to be truthful if each agent
C2.4.note: Ballots b are notated separately from preferences ≻.

C3.1.quote: agents can successively deviate from their current submitted ballot
C3.1.note: All main analyses concern the iterative winner after strategic deviations. The initial profile is truthful.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH. No utility notions are used for voters.

C5.1.note: Condorcet/Borda winners serve only as target candidates. They are not used as welfare criteria.

VOT.quote_behav: A voter i deviates from ballot bti to ballot
VOT.quote_info: we assume that voters only have partial knowledge about the other ballots
VOT.note: Myopic best-response or veto-winner deviations, made when the voter believes she is pivotal. The initial ballot is truthful.

ORG.note: No election authority or chair acts in the model; the polling agency is coded under BRI.

BRI.quote_behav: the polling agency tries to make some distinguished candidate win
BRI.quote_info: reasonable to assume complete information for the polling agency, since it collects
BRI.note: The polling agency is an external manipulator, not a voter and not the election authority. It manipulates the announced poll to reach a constructive or destructive goal.

C7.1.note: Both voters and polling agency are strategic.

C8.1.quote: We consider a strategic game called iterative voting
C8.1.note: Voters follow iterative best-response or veto-winner dynamics. The polling agency's manipulation is studied as a decision problem.

C9.2.quote: The voters trust the results communicated by the polling agency

C6.BRI.reason: The polling agency only announces poll results and is not the organiser or election authority, so it fits the external-manipulator type BRI rather than ORG.

C6.ORG.reason: No organiser or chair chooses anything in the model, and the polling agency is an external manipulator rather than the election authority.
